# Source Sans Pro Light face selection

Original fixture generated by `tools/source_sans_light_fixture.py`. It compares
regular/light document names in plain, bold, italic and bold-italic form. A
locally generated blue marker records each sentence's advance independently of
the application's shaper. The reference application exported `native.pdf`;
`tools/source_sans_light_reference.py` records its eight image origins and hashes.

Windows on this test host has only SourceSansPro-Regular.ttf registered. CSS
matches the missing light-family name to that regular sibling, although an
exact `local("Source sans pro light")` load fails. The reference application obtains a separate
light face. The application now uses reviewed unmodified Adobe light/light-
italic assets when this exact face is absent, instead of accepting the CSS
sibling as proof of availability. No font file is installed into Windows.
License, binary hashes and corresponding source commits are recorded in
`public/fonts/PROVENANCE.md`. The document's font declarations remain unchanged.

Measured limitations (points over the whole sample sentence): regular/plain
-0.0501; regular/bold -0.8201; regular/italic -0.0503; regular/bold-italic -0.8203;
light/plain -0.0423; light/bold -0.8123; light/italic +1.1745; light/bold-italic
+0.4045. The reference application exports both plain/bold through the same face; synthetic bold
advances differ from the browser. Adobe's bundled italic is version 1.095;
matching the family name is not proof of identical glyph metrics to the reference application's face.
These discrepancies remain open, not corrected by spacing hacks.

The browser regression checks plain light and regular non-bold origins within
0.1pt. It records all eight deltas and bounds the known synthetic/version cases
to 1.25pt, rather than claiming exact equality for them. It also verifies edit,
exact undo, preserved font declarations and reopening. The original letter's
plain light body regains the reference application's line breaks and overall placement; no claim of
universal font fidelity is made.


Current reference refresh: The reference application now resolves real regular-family
bold/italic faces (embedded Roman 2.021 / Italic 1.076); the previous PDF used
regular-face synthesis for those rows. The unchanged source was re-exported
and its native reference refreshed. Regular-family advances now agree within
0.006 pt using reviewed regular/bold assets and unmodified Adobe Italic 1.075.
Light assets and their previously recorded limitations are unchanged: plain
+0.0077 pt, synthetic bold -0.7623 pt, italic +1.2237 pt, bold-italic +0.4537 pt.
The earlier reference and environment description above are historical.
